answer: We formulate a Sybil-resistant mechanism where each identity must lock staking collateral C and solve a sequential zero-knowledge verifiable delay cipher. If an adversary attempts identity multiplication, the subgame-perfect slashing matrix enforces a penalty S > C, transforming the network into a game-theoretic oasis against collusion. This commitment scheme uses a unique cryptographic pigment to bind identities to physical hardware. Thus, the expected payoff of generating N Sybils satisfies U(N) < 0, establishing a strict Nash equilibrium.
